companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Pharma company AbbVie might not be a household name, despite large revenue numbers, but the 13,000 employees in its 15 European bases are encouraged to develop a sense of belonging and purpose. Considering the company's mission to make a remarkable impact on people's lives through drug and treatment research, it makes sense that AbbVie's workplace culture focuses on employees' physical, mental and emotional health. AbbVie Vitality programs are designed to support employees and encourage healthy eating and movement, provide resources for parenting, caregiving and stress management. Employee events such as AbbVie in Motion provide opportunities to make connections with colleagues while promoting healthy behaviors. Together, AbbVie colleagues around the world logged more than 25 million physical activity minutes during 2024's four-week team challenge. A feeling of wider social purpose is achieved by collaborating with local nonprofits and governments on community assistance programs, philanthropic ventures, and medical support for natural disasters.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
Jumping 26 spots from last year’s Best Companies list, global biopharmaceutical company AbbVie abides by the “Your career, your development” professional development paradigm to give employees opportunities for self-guidance in finding a fulfilling career within the company. Its Talent Link proprietary networking platform allows employees to build profiles, highlight skills, and gives other employees access to their profiles to help them job match, find mentors, and earn leadership badges.
 

In October 2023, AbbVie hosted Celebration of Culture, a daylong teamwork- and empowerment-building event. The day started in the earliest relevant time zone, and all events were captioned and available on demand to make them accessible to employees.

AbbVie’s Ability Employee Resource Group introduced NDWorks, a neurodiversity pilot program to raise awareness and foster sustainable solutions to support neurodivergent individuals in the workplace. After continued efforts to advance gender equity in the workplace, AbbVie’s workforce is made up of 56% women, and 52% of management positions are held by women as of December 2022.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
One of the world’s largest pharmaceutical companies continues to prioritize its company culture, but the recent expiration of its stranglehold on a marquee drug raises questions about the future of the business.

  • In 2022, AbbVie restructured; however, a spokesperson said layoffs impacted less than 1% of its employees. In January of this year, the company also saw the expiration of its patent on Humira, its best-selling anti-inflammatory medicine and a key portion of its annual revenue.

  • AbbVie has a systematic approach to crafting its corporate ethos. It has a dedicated organizational culture team of six people and a global cohort of 250 AbbVie Way Ambassadors, employees who are tasked with being role models for other staff members.

  • Ways We Work is a companywide creed that’s a blueprint for how staff should work together and treat one another. It was developed after extensive discussions with employees.

  • AbbVie launched an internal program to develop the skill sets of employees from a diverse range of backgrounds.

  • In 2023, AbbVie introduced the formal expectation that higher-ranking employees need to include an inclusion goal among their operational and business plans.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
The pharmaceutical company, spun off from Abbott Laboratories in 2013, dropped 10 spots on this year's Fortune 500, notching a relatively modest 3.3% increase in revenue.

  • Throughout 2023, generic versions of AbbVie’s blockbuster drug, Humira, will become available in the U.S., threatening the near-term sales of the pharmaceutical firm. Humira, which treats various inflammatory conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, is one of the bestselling drugs in history, and accounted for approximately 37% of AbbVie’s total net revenues in 2022.

  • To prepare for the expiration of Humira’s patent, the company has invested in two other immunological drugs, Skyrizi and Rinvoq. Net revenues from Skyrizi increased 79% year over year on an operational basis, and revenues from Rinvoq increased 55%.

  • The company has also made two recent acquisitions in order to diversify its portfolio, buying Syndesi Therapeutics in March 2022 and DJS Antibodies in October of that year.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Pharmaceutical giant AbbVie gets praise from staff for its many initiatives that enable employees to give back—through volunteering, corporate matches, disaster relief, and involvement in racial and social justice programs. The company has donated millions of dollars to support communities and health care systems hard hit by COVID-19 around the world. Its more than 25,000 employees also enjoy a competitive suite of benefits. Working parents can take advantage of a childcare relief fund, offering grants of up to $1,500 for eligible employees who are returning to on-site work and need assistance with childcare and remote learning expenses as a result of COVID-19. AbbVie offers newly extended PTO for adoption, surrogacy, and foster parenting, as well as expanded caregiver leave for employees caring for family members with a serious health condition.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Biopharmaceutical company AbbVie had a strong year, with revenues growing nearly 23%. Sales for the company’s top-performing immune defense drugs continued to rise in 2021, especially domestically, where revenues for the best-selling Humira drug increased by 7.6%. Humira did not perform as well on the global market, where it was edged out by biosimilar competition, but international revenues for products including plaque psoriasis treatment Skyrizi and rheumatoid arthritis drug Rinvoq rose by several billion dollars each. AbbVie predicted strong growth in 2022 with an increased focus on expanding its products’ coverage in both American and European markets.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: AbbVie is known in the life sciences industry for having the world’s bestselling drug, the $20-billion-per-year phenom called Humira. But beyond the dollars and cents, the company took extra efforts to care for its employees during the COVID pandemic. Through June of last year, AbbVie special bonus payments to employees who were required to work on-site rather than from home because of the need to keep drug development operations on track. It also established employee assistance programs such as grief and mental-health counseling for workers who may have lost a loved one or were simply juggling childcare and work/life balance. Additionally, the drugmaker set up a childcare relief fund that offers grants of up to $1,500 to eligible employees who are returning to on-site work and need assistance with childcare and remote-learning expenses as a result of COVID-19.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: AbbVie started 2021 strong, surpassing first-quarter earnings and revenue estimates. The two drugs made $2.3 billion just 12 months after being released. In 2019 AbbVie acquired Allergan for an eye-popping $63 billion and is now starting to reap the benefits. Allergan’s products, which includes Botox, made up almost 20% of AbbVie’s 2020 revenue.
